extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent applicants and practitioners (agents/attorneys) seeking to use the Global/IP5 PPH pilot program
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and filing a request to participate in the USPTO's Global/IP5 Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) pilot programs, including eligibility conditions, required documents, submission procedures, and special examining procedures. Focused on procedural and substantive requirements applicants must meet to obtain accelerated prosecution based on foreign or PCT work products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose/benefits of PPH
rubrics_metrics.description: The PPH enables an applicant who receives a positive ruling on patent claims from one participating office to request accelerated prosecution of corresponding claims in another participating office; it promotes processing efficiency by allowing the office of later examination (OLE) to reuse the search and examination results from the office of earlier examination (OEE), thereby reducing workload and duplication of effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains rationale for using PPH: obtain a patentability decision more quickly and leverage OEE work products. (Background/contextual guidance; not an eligibility requirement.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Same earliest date requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The U.S. application for which participation in the Global/IP5 PPH pilot program is requested must have the same earliest date, whether this is the priority date or filing date, as that of a corresponding national or regional application filed with another Global/IP5 PPH participating office, or a corresponding PCT international application for which one of the Global/IP5 PPH participating offices was the ISA or the IPEA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Earliest date equality is required between the U.S. application and the corresponding application or PCT where the participating office acted as ISA/IPEA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corresponding application must have at least one allowable/patentable claim
rubrics_metrics.description: The corresponding application has at least one claim indicated by the OEE in its capacity as a national or regional Office, ISA, or IPEA to be allowable/patentable. A claim determined as novel, inventive, and industrially applicable by the ISA or IPEA has the meaning of allowable/patentable for the purposes of this program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An explicit positive indication from the OEE (including PCT work products) that at least one claim is allowable/patentable is required to base the PPH request on.

rubrics_metrics.name: All U.S. claims must sufficiently correspond to OEE allowable/patentable claims
rubrics_metrics.description: All claims in the U.S. application for which participation is requested must sufficiently correspond to the allowable/patentable claims in the corresponding OEE application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines 'sufficiently correspond': accounting for differences due to claim format requirements, the claim is of the same or similar scope as an allowable/patentable claim in the OEE. A narrower U.S. claim can sufficiently correspond if presented as dependent on a claim of same/similar scope. A claim that introduces a new/different category (e.g., product claims when OEE had only process claims) is not considered to sufficiently correspond. Example and explanation of narrower-scope claims and dependent-claim strategy are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination must not have begun
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive examination of the U.S. application for which participation in the Global/IP5 PPH pilot program is requested has not begun.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If substantive examination has already started, the application is not eligible for PPH participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request form and advance out of turn; no petition fee required
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must submit a request for participation in the Global/IP5 PPH pilot program and a request that the U.S. application be advanced out of turn for examination by order of the Director to expedite the business of the Office under 37 CFR 1.102(a). A request form is available from the USPTO Web site. A petition fee under 37 CFR 1.17(h) is NOT required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the USPTO PPH request form (URL provided). No petition fee (per cited Federal Register notice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims correspondence table in English
rubrics_metrics.description: A claims correspondence table in English, indicating how and certifying that all the claims in the U.S. application correspond to allowable/patentable claims in the OEE application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The table must certify correspondence and be in English. It is an essential documentary requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy of OEE office action or PCT work product (with translation) or identify if accessible
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the office action issued just prior to the 'Decision to Grant a Patent' (e.g., the latest 'Notification of Reasons for Refusal') in the OEE national/regional application, along with an English translation thereof, if applicable, or the latest work product in the international phase of the OEE PCT application (e.g., the Written Opinion of the ISA or, where a demand under PCT Chapter II has been filed, the Written Opinion of the IPEA or the International Preliminary Examination Report), along with an English translation thereof, if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the office action or PCT work product is already present in the U.S. application or is available via specified dossier access systems (JPO Dossier Access or WIPO PATENTSCOPE), the applicant must identify the document but need not supply a copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Disclosure Statement (IDS) listing cited documents and copies
rubrics_metrics.description: An information disclosure statement listing the documents cited in the office action or PCT work product submitted, along with copies of all documents except U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications. Any IDS or document copies submitted in the U.S. application prior to the Global/IP5 PPH request need not be resubmitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IDS must include the documents cited in the OEE work product; copies required except for U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission via EFS-Web and document indexing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The above-listed documents must be submitted via EFS-Web and indexed with the document description 'Petition to make special under the Patent Pros Hwy,' except that any preliminary amendment or IDS submitted with the PPH request must be separately indexed as a preliminary amendment or an IDS, respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow EFS-Web upload and correct document description/indexing conventions to ensure proper processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to perfect defective requests but examination not suspended
rubrics_metrics.description: If the request does not meet all requirements, the applicant will be notified and defects identified and given one opportunity to perfect the request in a renewed request for participation. Action on the application by the USPTO will NOT be suspended (37 CFR 1.103) awaiting a renewed request. If the application is picked up for examination after notification of defects, any renewed request will be dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You have one chance to fix defects before your renewed request may be dismissed if examination has started. If perfected and examination has not begun, special status will be granted and the application advanced out of turn; if not perfected, the application waits in its regular turn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special status carryover rules (RCE but not continuing application)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for participation in the Global/IP5 PPH pilot program and special status granted in an application carries over to a request for continued examination (RCE) of the application, but a request granted in a parent application will not carry over to a continuing application. The applicant must fulfill all conditions set forth above for special status to be granted in a continuing application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RCEs inherit PPH status; continuations do not — separate PPH requests and fulfillment of conditions are required for continuing applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments or newly added claims after grant must correspond and require certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Any claims amended or added after the grant of the request for participation must sufficiently correspond to one or more allowable/patentable claims in the OEE application. The applicant is required to submit, along with the amendment, a statement certifying that the amended or newly added claims sufficiently correspond to the allowable/patentable claims in the OEE application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the certification statement is omitted, the amendment will not be entered and will be treated as a non-responsive reply. This is treated strictly to preserve PPH eligibility after changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPH does not absolve duty of candor and disclosure (37 CFR 1.56 and 37 CFR 11.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Global/IP5 PPH pilot program does not absolve applicants of all their duties under 37 CFR 1.56 and 37 CFR 11.18. By complying with requirements to submit OEE documents and an IDS, the applicant would be considered to have complied with the duty to bring to the attention of the USPTO any material prior art cited in corresponding foreign applications, but the applicant still has a duty of candor and good faith, including providing to the USPTO other information known to be material to patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting OEE work products helps meet the duty to submit prior art cited abroad, but applicants must still disclose any other material information and comply with ethical duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot trial period and termination/extension criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The Global PPH pilot program commenced January 6, 2014 and will run for one year; the IP5 PPH pilot program commenced January 6, 2014 and will run for three years. The trial period for each pilot program may be extended if necessary. The participating offices may terminate either pilot early if the volume of participation exceeds a manageable level, or for any other reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs are time-limited trials subject to extension or early termination; notice will be published if terminated.
